identity.title: Orthostatic vitals: SBP drop >=20 / DBP >=10 mmHg or pulse increment >=30/min at 1-3 min standing

technique.how: Measure BP and pulse after >=2 min supine (or 5 min if possible), then stand the patient and repeat at 1 min and 3 min, asking about dizziness. Positive: SBP fall >=20 mmHg or DBP fall >=10 mmHg, pulse rise >=30/min, or inability to stand because of severe dizziness. Count the pulse for a full 30 s; supine-to-sitting is a weaker substitute.
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to stand with assistance; note beta-blockers, pacemaker, and autonomic disease which blunt the pulse response.
technique.contraindications: Do not stand a patient who is frankly hypotensive, syncopal, or at high fall risk without support.

interpretation.positive_finding: A postural pulse increment >=30/min or severe postural dizziness is highly specific (98%) for large acute blood loss and supports hypovolemia; a postural SBP drop meeting criteria supports orthostatic hypotension as a cause of syncope or dizziness. In the elderly a positive test is common and may reflect drugs or autonomic failure rather than volume loss.
interpretation.negative_finding: A normal test does not exclude moderate hypovolemia (sensitivity only 22% after ~450-630 mL loss) and does not exclude cardiac syncope.
interpretation.pitfalls: Supine hypotension and tachycardia are insensitive even after >1 L blood loss; beta-blockade and pacing abolish the pulse rise; mild dizziness alone has no proven value; timing matters (measure at 1 and 3 min).
interpretation.changes_what: A large pulse increment or severe postural dizziness should raise hypovolemia/hemorrhage to the top and trigger volume resuscitation and source search; a normal test should not stop the workup.

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolemia from large acute blood loss (630-1150 mL phlebotomy)
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing controlled phlebotomy (pooled volunteer studies); finding = postural pulse increment >=30/min OR severe postural dizziness preventing upright vital signs
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.97/(1-0.98) = 48.5; LR- = (1-0.97)/0.98 = 0.03; from abstract sensitivity 97% and specificity 98%
estimates.quote: a much greater sensitivity for large blood loss of 97% (95% CI, 91%-100%); the corresponding specificity is 98% (95% CI, 97%-99%)

estimates.target_condition: Hypovolemia from moderate acute blood loss (450-630 mL phlebotomy)
estimates.population: Healthy adult volunteers undergoing controlled phlebotomy (pooled volunteer studies); finding = postural pulse increment >=30/min OR severe postural dizziness
estimates.computed_from: LR+ = 0.22/(1-0.98) = 11; LR- = (1-0.22)/0.98 = 0.80; from abstract sensitivity 22% and specificity 98%
estimates.quote: sensitivity for moderate blood loss of only 22% (95% confidence interval [CI], 6%-48%) ... the corresponding specificity is 98% (95% CI, 97%-99%)

sources.citation: McGee S, Abernethy WB 3rd, Simel DL. The rational clinical examination. Is this patient hypovolemic? JAMA. 1999;281(11):1022-1029.
Albassam OT, Redelmeier RJ, Shadowitz S, Husain AM, Simel D, Etchells EE. Did This Patient Have Cardiac Syncope?: The Rational Clinical Examination Systematic Review. JAMA. 2019;321(24):2448-2457.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not stand a patient with supine hypotension, active hemorrhage, or suspected acute cardiac event to obtain orthostatics; the information is not worth the fall/syncope risk.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Inability to stand because of dizziness, or a pulse increment >=30/min, in a patient with possible bleeding indicates large-volume loss and warrants immediate resuscitation and source control.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Reproducibility depends on standing duration and pulse-counting method; the RCE notes a supine period of at least 2 min and standing measurements at 1 min are needed for valid results.

extraction_notes: Sens/spec entered as percent. Both estimates are the composite finding (pulse increment >=30/min or severe postural dizziness) in volunteer phlebotomy models, not ED patients; the RCE abstract also states supine hypotension has sensitivity 33% (21-47) after up to 1150 mL loss and that mild postural dizziness has no proven value, but gives no numbers for the postural SBP-drop criterion (>=20 mmHg) in the abstract and the JAMA full text is not accessible, so no BP-drop estimate is entered. For the syncope indication, the 2019 cardiac-syncope RCE (source 1) abstract contains no orthostatic-vital-sign estimate; it is cited as context that orthostatic hypotension is a non-cardiac cause and the test does not rule out cardiac syncope. No ED cohort with a reference standard for hypovolemia was found in the abstract-level search.
